name: Andrew Bosworth

summary.text: Andrew "Boz" Bosworth is Meta's chief technology officer and head of Reality Labs, the wearables and metaverse organization he established in 2017; he joined Facebook as an engineer in 2006 and became CTO in 2022. He is the named inventor on US patent 12,513,102 B2, "Simulation of a user of a social networking system using a language model", filed November 29, 2023 and issued December 30, 2025 to Meta Platforms Technologies LLC, which describes training a language model on a user's own interactions to simulate the user when absent, including if deceased.

facts.claim: Meta's executive biography describes Bosworth as Chief Technology Officer and Head of Reality Labs, the company's wearables and metaverse organization, which he established in 2017.
facts.quote: Andrew Bosworth—or Boz, as most people know him—is Chief Technology Officer at Meta, and Head of Reality Labs, the company's wearables and metaverse organization which he established in 2017.

facts.claim: Bosworth joined Facebook in 2006 as an early engineer and, per Meta's bio, built the original News Feed, Messenger and Groups, and ran the Ads and Business Platform group before Reality Labs.
facts.quote: He built the original News Feed, Messenger, Groups, as well as many early anti-abuse and infrastructure systems.

facts.claim: The patent's abstract and description state that the language model, trained on the user's interactions, may simulate the user when absent from the social networking system, for example during a long break or if the user is deceased.
facts.quote: The language model may be used for simulating the user when the user is absent from the social networking system, for example, when the user takes a long break or if the user is deceased

facts.claim: Coverage of the patent reports that the simulated user could post, comment and interact across Facebook, Instagram and Threads, and that the filing does not detail how a user would authorize posthumous simulation.
